note: Which receiver a deep link must be built against. Published as data so a consumer reads it instead of hard-coding a route, and so a retired route can be retired once, here, rather than in every dashboard that ever copied it.
why_this_file_exists: On 2026-09-05 the MAP button in Pipeline News v9.7 was measured pointing at https://globalgrid2050.com/repd_grid_atlasv8/ - a page carrying zero engine cartridges and no current.json, so no deep link arriving there could ever compute a nearest substation, a corridor estimate or a rating envelope. It was not intermittent and it was not a browser fault: the route was hard-coded in the consumer, in atlasUrlV9_5_1(), and the engine published no statement of which receiver was canonical for it to disagree with.

canonical.evidence: The served shell references the composition manifest (current.json) and its cartridges; measured 2026-09-05, 20 cartridge references and 3 current.json references in the shell.
computes: nearest transmission substation at 400 kV and above
arrival identity from the REPD reference

retired.reason: The V8 overlay. It is a real page and it still serves, so a link to it does not 404 - which is why this was invisible. It carries no cartridge, no current.json and no nearest-substation path, so an arrival there is silently inert. Do not build a deep link against it. It remains published for readers who want the V8 map itself.

rule: Build every project deep link with buildDeepLink(project) and let the contract supply the base, or read canonical.route from this file. A consumer that hard-codes a receiver has taken on the job of noticing when that receiver stops carrying the engine, and no consumer in this estate has ever noticed.
